paper.title_en: Information geometry of continuum limits in lattice field theory: The Gross-Neveu model with Wilson fermions
paper.abstract_en: When the Boltzmann weight is nonnegative, the actions of a lattice field theory form a statistical manifold, whose Fisher metric gives the number of measurements needed to distinguish two nearby actions. For the two-dimensional lattice Gross-Neveu model with Wilson fermions in the large-$N$ limit, we study the continuum limit, in which the lattice spacing $a$ goes to zero at fixed mass gap $Λ$, through the Fisher metric of the distribution of the auxiliary field $σ$. The renormalization condition fixes an expectation coordinate, and dimensional transmutation becomes an exponential relation between it and a natural coordinate. The main result is that the $a\to0$ limits differ between the Fisher metric of the long-distance modes, whose momenta are fixed in physical units, and that of the full $P(σ)$. In the former, the infinitely many irrelevant directions that change the kinetic term locally shrink relative to the mass-term direction to order $aΛ\log(1/(aΛ))$ or smaller, and several modes together leave only the two directions $(Λ,m)$ of the continuum theory. In the latter, the kinetic-term directions shrink as fast as the mass-term direction, and the difference in the regularization remains in lattice-scale correlations. In the eight-dimensional space of local deformations examined numerically, the one exception is the deformation that only adds a contact term to the propagator, which as $a\to0$ becomes indistinguishable from a change of $1/g^2$ in both metrics. In the Fisher metric of the full $P(σ)$, the curvature of the coupling plane at fixed kinetic term diverges as $(1/2)\log^2(1/(aΛ))$, not as the correlation volume often assumed in thermodynamic geometry, and the critical point lies at infinite distance in this plane.
